info.description:
# Cubbo Clients API

The client-facing fulfillment API: create and track orders, manage inventory and replenishments, handle returns, and receive outbound webhooks.

| Environment | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| Production | `https://api.cubbo.com/v1` |
| Staging | `https://api-staging.cubbo.com/v1` |

## Setup

Set two Postman **environment** variables:

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `clients_api_url` | `https://api.cubbo.com/v1` (or the staging URL) |
| `clients_api_bearer_token` | the `token` returned by `POST /auth/token` |

Every request inherits collection-level Bearer auth from `clients_api_bearer_token` — don't set an `Authorization` header per request.

## Quickstart

1. `POST /auth/token` with your `client_id` / `client_secret` → `{ token, expires_in, type }`.
    
2. **Cache the token** and reuse it until it is close to expiry (default 24 h). There are no refresh tokens, and re-authenticating on every call is the most common way to hit the rate limits.
    
3. Call any endpoint with `Authorization: Bearer` .
    
4. For order/shipping/inventory state changes, subscribe to the outbound events in the **Webhooks** folder instead of polling.
    

## Pagination

List endpoints take `page` (default `1`) and `per_page` (default `10`), and return a `meta` object alongside the data:

``` json
{
  "current_page": 1,
  "next_page": 2,
  "prev_page": null,
  "total_pages": 9,
  "first_page": true,
  "last_page": false,
  "per_page": 10,
  "total_count": 84
}

 ```

`per_page` caps differ per endpoint:

| Endpoint | Max `per_page` | Over the max |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /orders` | 100 | silently clamped to 100 |
| `GET /orders/with-fields` | 100 | `422` |
| `GET /orders/awaiting-invoice` | 100 | `422` |
| `GET /returns/awaiting-invoice` | 100 | `422` |
| `GET /inventory` | 200 | `422` |
| `GET /lots` | 200 | `422` |

**Detecting the last page:** use `next_page == null`. Do not rely on `last_page` — when a query returns no results at all, `total_pages` is `0` and `last_page` is `false`.

## Status codes, errors and rate limits

See the **Errors** folder.

request.description:
This endpoint issues an OAuth2 **client_credentials** access token. Send your `client_id` and `client_secret`; you receive a Bearer token used to authenticate every other request in this API.

Auth follows the Bearer token standard: https://swagger.io/docs/specification/authentication/bearer-authentication/

### Request body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `client_id` | string | yes | Your API client id. |
| `client_secret` | string | yes | Your API client secret. |
| `expires_in` | integer | no | Token lifetime in seconds (min `10`, max `86400`). Defaults to `86400` (24 h). |
| `grant_type` | string | no | OAuth2 grant type. Defaults to `client_credentials`, which is the only supported value. |

### Response

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `token` | The Bearer access token. Send it on every request as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. |
| `expires_in` | Seconds until the token expires. |
| `type` | Always `Bearer`. |

### Token renewal

There are **no refresh tokens**. When a token expires (after `expires_in` seconds) request a new one by calling this endpoint again with your `client_id` / `client_secret`. Cache and reuse a token until it is close to expiry rather than requesting a new one on every call.

### Rate limit

This endpoint allows **60 token requests per minute per `client_id`**, and **30 requests per 30 seconds per source IP** — exceeding the IP limit blocks your IP for 10 minutes. Cache and reuse a token instead of requesting one per call. See **Errors → Rate limits**.

request.description:
### Description

Creates a new fulfillment order in the Cubbo platform. The order is validated, persisted, and queued for asynchronous processing (stock assignment, shipping label generation, etc.).

**Note:** For Brazil orders, use `POST /v1/brazil/orders` instead — it requires fiscal fields (tax_id, billing, prices per item).

### Authentication

```
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>

 ```

Obtain the token via `POST /v1/auth/token` using your `client_id` and `client_secret`.

### Headers

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer` |

### Parameters

#### Root Level

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `store_id` | Integer | Yes | ID of the store where the order will be created. |
| `order_number` | String | Yes | Unique order identifier. Must not already exist for the given store. |
| `shipping_method_id` | Integer | Conditional | ID of the shipping method. Required if `shipping_line_code` is not provided. |
| `shipping_line_code` | String | Conditional | Integration shipping method name. Required if `shipping_method_id` is not provided. |
| `is_paid` | Boolean | No | Whether the order has been paid. Defaults to `true`. |
| `is_click_and_collect` | Boolean | No | Whether this is a click & collect order. Defaults to `false`. |
| `click_and_collect_service_code` | String | No | Service code for click & collect. Only applies when `is_click_and_collect` is `true`. |
| `channel_name` | String | No | Name of the sales channel (e.g., "shopify", "mercadolibre"). |
| `channel_order_id` | String | No | Order ID in the external sales channel. |
| `has_carrier_insurance` | Boolean | No | **Chile only.** Declares the order's value to the carrier so the shipment travels insured. Defaults to `false`. See **Carrier insurance (Chile)** below. |
| `is_cod` | Boolean | No | Whether the carrier collects payment from the recipient at delivery (cash on delivery). Defaults to `false`. See **Cash on delivery** below. |
| `cod_amount` | Decimal | No | **Chile only.** The amount to collect at delivery when it differs from the order's value — a partial collection. Omit it to collect the order's full value. See **Cash on delivery** below. |
| `requires_document_return` | Boolean | No | **Chile only.** Asks the carrier to carry a sheet the recipient signs at delivery and bring it back to you. Defaults to `false`. See **Signed-document return (Chile)** below. |
| `requires_pickup_on_delivery` | Boolean | No | **Chile only, consumer orders only.** Ships a second Blue Express label inside the package so the recipient can send a return later. Defaults to `false`. See **Return label (Chile)** below. |

#### `shipping` Object (Required)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `first_name` | String | Yes | Recipient first name. |
| `last_name` | String | No | Recipient last name. |
| `phone` | String | Yes | Recipient phone number. |
| `email` | String | Yes | Recipient email address. |
| `address1` | String | Yes | Primary street address. |
| `address2` | String | No | Secondary address (apartment, suite, etc.). |
| `references` | String | No | Delivery references or instructions. |
| `number` | String | No | Street number. |
| `country` | String | Yes | Country code (ISO alpha-2, e.g., `"MX"`). |
| `city` | String | Yes | City name. |
| `province` | String | Yes | State or province name. |
| `zip_code` | String | Conditional | Postal code. Required depending on warehouse country configuration. |

#### `billing` Object (Optional)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `first_name` | String | Yes\* | Billing first name. |
| `last_name` | String | Yes\* | Billing last name. |
| `phone` | String | Yes\* | Billing phone number. |
| `email` | String | Yes\* | Billing email address. |
| `address1` | String | Yes\* | Billing street address. |
| `address2` | String | No | Secondary billing address. |
| `address3` | String | No | Third billing address line. |
| `country` | String | Yes\* | Billing country code. |
| `city` | String | Yes\* | Billing city. |
| `province` | String | Yes\* | Billing state or province. |
| `zip_code` | String | No | Billing postal code. |

\*Required only when the `billing` object is included.

#### `products` Array (Required)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sku` | String | Yes | Product SKU. Must exist in the specified store. |
| `quantity` | Integer | Yes | Quantity of units to fulfill. |

### `shipping_documents` Array (Optional)

Attach documents (shipping labels, invoices, etc.) to the order at creation time. Each document can be provided either as a URL or as base64-encoded data.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | String | Yes | The document content. Either a **public URL** to the PDF file, or a **base64-encoded** string of the file content. The interpretation depends on `document_type`. |
| `document_type` | String | Yes | Source type of the document. Determines how `data` is interpreted. Accepted values: `"url"`, `"base64"`. |
| `printing_type` | String | Yes | How the document should be printed/used. Accepted values: `"label"`, `"document"`, `"difal_bill"`, `"difal_payment_receipt"`, `"identifier_label"`, `"oxxo_digital_card"`. |
| `metadata` | Object | No | Additional key-value metadata to attach to the document. |

> Note: All documents are stored as PDF files regardless of source type. The content_type is automatically set to application/pdf.  
 
  

#### Example — Document from URL

```
{
  "shipping_documents": [
    {
      "data": "https://example.com/labels/order-123.pdf",
      "document_type": "url",
      "printing_type": "label"
    }
  ]
}

 ```

#### Example — Document from Base64

```
{
  "shipping_documents": [
    {
      "data": "JVBERi0xLjQKMSAwIG9iago8PAovVHlwZSAvQ2F0YWxvZw...",
      "document_type": "base64",
      "printing_type": "document",
      "metadata": {
        "invoice_number": "INV-001"
      }
    }
  ]
}

 ```

### Carrier insurance (Chile)

Setting `has_carrier_insurance` to `true` marks the order so that Cubbo declares its value to the carrier when the shipping guide is emitted, and the shipment travels insured. Available for **Chilean warehouses only**.

The order is rejected at creation if any of the following is not met:

| Requirement | Error code returned |
| --- | --- |
| The order's warehouse is in Chile | `CARRIER_INSURANCE_NOT_AVAILABLE` |
| The order has a value greater than zero | `MISSING_INSURANCE_VALUE` |
| The order's currency is the warehouse country's currency (`CLP`) | `INSURANCE_CURRENCY_MISMATCH` |

**The shipping method is checked later, not at creation.** If the method cannot carry the service — Cubbo must emit the guide for it, so pickups are excluded, as are methods where you supply your own guide — the order is accepted here and then fails validation during processing: it lands in `error` status carrying `INSURANCE_SHIPPING_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED`. Read the order back to see it.

**The insured value comes from your product prices.** This endpoint has no `total_price` field: the order's value is calculated from the prices of the products it contains, as they are registered in Cubbo. If those products have no price, the value is zero and an insured order is rejected with `MISSING_INSURANCE_VALUE`. Register your product prices before insuring — you can set them when creating or updating a product, or through your sales channel integration.

`has_carrier_insurance` is returned by `GET /orders` and `GET /orders/with-fields`, so you can confirm what was stored.

#### Example — insured Chilean order

```
{
  "store_id": 1234,
  "order_number": "ORD-00002",
  "shipping_method_id": 56,
  "has_carrier_insurance": true,
  "shipping": {
    "first_name": "Camila",
    "last_name": "Rojas",
    "phone": "+56912345678",
    "email": "camila@example.com",
    "address1": "Av. Providencia 1234",
    "country": "CL",
    "city": "Providencia",
    "province": "Region Metropolitana",
    "zip_code": "7500000"
  },
  "products": [
    {
      "sku": "SKU-001",
      "quantity": 1
    }
  ]
}

 ```

**What this field records.** The carrier prints nothing about the insurance on the label and returns nothing about it when the guide is emitted. This field therefore records the insurance requested for the shipment, not a confirmation from the carrier.

### Cash on delivery

Setting `is_cod` to `true` instructs the carrier to collect payment from the recipient when the order is delivered. Available in **Mexico, Colombia and Chile**.

By default the amount collected is the order's value, which comes from the prices of the products it contains — this endpoint has no `total_price` field, exactly as described under *Carrier insurance* above.

**Choosing a shipping method that can collect.** In Mexico and Colombia, collection is a property of the method: pick one whose `is_cod` is `true` in `GET /shipping-methods`. In Chile the ordinary method collects, so the method that will collect reports `is_cod: false` — that field names a dedicated cash-on-delivery method, not the capability. Do not use it alone to decide whether you may offer cash on delivery.

**Collecting a different amount (Chile).** `cod_amount` overrides the order's value when the recipient owes less than the order is worth — a partial collection, for instance when part was prepaid. It is the amount the carrier is instructed to collect, and it takes precedence over the order's value. Available for **Chilean warehouses only**.

- Omit `cod_amount`, or send `0`, to collect the order's full value. Zero reads as "no override", never as "collect nothing".
    
- The amount is rounded to the nearest whole unit before it reaches the carrier: currencies with no decimal subunit (`CLP`) carry no cents.
    

The order is rejected at creation if any of the following is not met:

| Requirement | Error code returned |
| --- | --- |
| The amount to collect is greater than zero | `MISSING_COD_VALUE` |
| `cod_amount` is sent only for a warehouse in a country that offers partial collection (Chile) | `COD_AMOUNT_NOT_AVAILABLE` |
| **Chile only:** the order's currency is the warehouse country's currency (`CLP`) | `COD_CURRENCY_MISMATCH` |

**The shipping method is checked later, not at creation**, exactly as described under *Carrier insurance* above: an order whose method cannot collect is accepted here and then lands in `error` status carrying `COD_SHIPPING_METHOD_EXPECTED`.

`is_cod` and `cod_amount` are returned by `GET /orders` and `GET /orders/with-fields`, so you can confirm what was stored.

**All four services are set at creation only.** `PUT /v1/orders/:id` does not accept `is_cod`, `cod_amount`, `has_carrier_insurance`, `requires_document_return` or `requires_pickup_on_delivery`, so an order's complementary services cannot be changed through this API once the order exists.

#### Example — Chilean order with a partial collection

```
{
  "store_id": 1234,
  "order_number": "ORD-00003",
  "shipping_method_id": 56,
  "is_cod": true,
  "cod_amount": 30000,
  "shipping": {
    "first_name": "Camila",
    "last_name": "Rojas",
    "phone": "+56912345678",
    "email": "camila@example.com",
    "address1": "Av. Providencia 1234",
    "country": "CL",
    "city": "Providencia",
    "province": "Region Metropolitana",
    "zip_code": "7500000"
  },
  "products": [
    {
      "sku": "SKU-001",
      "quantity": 1
    }
  ]
}

 ```

### Signed-document return (Chile)

Setting `requires_document_return` to `true` asks the carrier to carry a sheet with the shipment, have the recipient sign it at delivery, and bring it back to you as proof. Available for **Chilean warehouses only**.

Unlike the two services above, nothing here is denominated: there is no amount, no currency, and therefore no value requirement and no currency check.

The order is rejected at creation if the following is not met:

| Requirement | Error code returned |
| --- | --- |
| The order's warehouse is in Chile | `DOCUMENT_RETURN_NOT_AVAILABLE` |

**The shipping method is checked later, not at creation**, as above: an order whose method cannot carry the service is accepted here and then lands in `error` status carrying `DOCUMENT_RETURN_SHIPPING_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED`.

**One sheet per shipment, not per package.** A multi-package order produces a single signature sheet for the whole shipment. Measured on a three-package order: the label PDF came back with four pages — three labels and one sheet.

**Where the sheet arrives.** It is an extra page inside the same label PDF the order already produces, so whoever prints the label gets the sheet with it. A single-package order with the service returns a two-page PDF instead of one page. This also makes the service the only one of the three you can verify from what the carrier returns: insurance and collection leave nothing in the emission response, but the sheet is visibly there in the PDF.

**Business shipments.** Blue Express offers this service for business deliveries, and Cubbo's own order form only offers it on B2B orders. This endpoint does not check an order's classification, so the request is accepted either way — confirm with your Cubbo contact before relying on it for consumer deliveries.

`requires_document_return` is returned by `GET /orders` and `GET /orders/with-fields`, so you can confirm what was stored.

#### Example — Chilean order with a signed-document return

```
{
  "store_id": 1234,
  "order_number": "ORD-00004",
  "shipping_method_id": 56,
  "is_b2b": true,
  "requires_document_return": true,
  "shipping": {
    "first_name": "Camila",
    "last_name": "Rojas",
    "phone": "+56912345678",
    "email": "camila@example.com",
    "address1": "Av. Providencia 1234",
    "country": "CL",
    "city": "Providencia",
    "province": "Region Metropolitana",
    "zip_code": "7500000"
  },
  "products": [
    {
      "sku": "SKU-001",
      "quantity": 1
    }
  ]
}

 ```

### Return label (Chile)

Setting `requires_pickup_on_delivery` to `true` ships a **second Blue Express label inside the package**, so the recipient can send something back later without asking you for a label first. Available for **Chilean warehouses only**, and for **consumer (D2C) orders only**.

The label is a full second emission at the carrier, with origin and destination inverted: it travels from the recipient's address back to the warehouse. Nothing about it is denominated — no amount, no currency — and it carries no complementary services of its own.

**Consumer orders only, and this one is a hard rule.** Unlike the signed-document return, where B2B is what Blue Express offers but the API accepts either classification, here D2C is the contract: Blue Express states the service is for consumer deliveries, so a business order is refused rather than accepted with a warning. The check is made on what the order **will be**, not on what you asked for — a store that can only produce business orders is refused whatever `is_b2b` says, and for a store that produces both, leaving `is_b2b` out means a consumer order and is accepted.

The order is rejected at creation if any of the following is not met:

| Requirement | Error code returned |
| --- | --- |
| The store's warehouse is in Chile | `PICKUP_ON_DELIVERY_NOT_AVAILABLE` |
| The order resolves to a consumer (D2C) order | `PICKUP_ON_DELIVERY_B2B_UNSUPPORTED` |
| Cubbo has the Blue Express return service configured for Chile | `PICKUP_ON_DELIVERY_RETURN_METHOD_NOT_CONFIGURED` |

The last one is a configuration problem on Cubbo's side rather than something wrong with your request: the label is built from a dedicated Blue Express return service, and without it there is nothing to emit. It is checked here, at creation, rather than at packing, so you find out while you can still act on the order. If you see it, contact your Cubbo representative.

**The shipping method is checked later, not at creation**, as with the three services above: an order whose method cannot carry the service is accepted here and then lands in `error` status carrying `PICKUP_ON_DELIVERY_SHIPPING_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED`. Cubbo must emit the outbound guide for the service to be possible, so pickups are excluded, as are methods where you supply your own guide.

**One label per order, not per package.** A multi-package order produces a single return label for the whole order. Measured on a three-package order: the printed document came back with four pages — three dispatch guides and one return label — and the order carried exactly one return label at the carrier.

**Where the label arrives, and where it does not.** It is an extra page inside the same label PDF the order already produces, so whoever packs the order gets it with the dispatch guides and puts it in the box. It is **not** returned by `GET /orders/:order_id/shipping-labels` or `GET /shipping-labels/:id`, and it does not appear in the order payload's label lists or on the tracking page: it is the recipient's label to use later, not a guide for this shipment, so those responses would misreport what is being dispatched.

**Using the label.** The recipient sends the parcel back with it and the warehouse recognises the guide on arrival, which opens a customer return against the original order. An unused label costs nothing and expires unused — it is inert until someone hands the parcel to Blue Express.

`requires_pickup_on_delivery` is returned by `GET /orders` and `GET /orders/with-fields`, so you can confirm what was stored. Like its three siblings, it is set at creation only.

request.description:
##### Order Statuses (status)

| **Status** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| initial | Has not been processed by the system. |
| unpaid | flagged as not paid yet. |
| empty | no products to ship |
| error | missing or invalid information on the order |
| entirely_dropshipping | no products to be fulfilled by Cubbo in this order. |
| backorder | not enough stock to fulfill the order. |
| pending | ready for processing. |
| processing | awating picker availability. |
| picking | order being picked. |
| packing | order awaiting packing. |
| shipped | order packing has concluded. |
| canceled | order was cancelled. |
| hold | order was paused. |
| interrupted | order was cancelled during processing, picking or packing. |
| returning | order is being returned. |
| returned | returning order was received at the warehouse. |
| return_arrived | order has arrived but is awaiting reception and processing by an operator |
| reentered | products received to the order have been returned to the warehouse |

##### Order Shipping Statuses (shipping_status)

| **Shipping Status** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| shipment_created | label acknowledged by carrier |
| shipment_collected | carrier has collected the package |
| shipment_in_transit | carrier delivery is in transit |
| shipment_delivered | carrier has delivered the package |
| shipment_canceled | delivery has been cancelled |
| shipment_returned | package was returned to origin |
| shipment_to_be_self_collected | package awating collection by receiver |
| shipment_out_for_delivery | package is being delivered |
| shipment_with_incident | carrier has reported an incident with the delivery |
| shipment_not_defined | carrier has reported an unknown delivery status |

##### Delivery Tracking (delivery_tracking)

Each order includes a `delivery_tracking` array with **one entry per package** (deduplicated by tracking number; a single-package order has one entry). The order also includes `is_multi_package` (boolean) indicating whether it ships as multiple independently-tracked packages.

| **Field** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| shipping_number | string or null | Carrier tracking/waybill number. |
| tracking_url | string or null | Carrier tracking URL. |
| cubbo_tracking_url | string | Cubbo-hosted tracking URL. |
| service_id | string or null | Carrier service identifier. |
| shipping_status | string or null | The package's shipping status (see shipping_status values above). |
| package_index | integer | 1-based index of this package within the order. |
| total_packages | integer | Total number of packages in the order. |

**The return label is not a package.** An order that shipped with `requires_pickup_on_delivery` carries a second Blue Express label inside the box, for the recipient to send a return later. It is not a package of this shipment, so it is absent from `delivery_tracking` and does not count towards `total_packages` or `is_multi_package` — a single-package order with the service still reports one entry.

##### Complementary services

Each order also carries the complementary services requested from the carrier at creation time.

| **Field** | **Type** | **Description** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| is_cod | boolean | The carrier collects payment from the recipient at delivery. Mexico, Colombia and Chile. |
| cod_amount | decimal or null | The amount the carrier is instructed to collect when it differs from the order's value — a partial collection. `null` means no override, so the order's full value is collected. Chile only. |
| has_carrier_insurance | boolean | The shipment's value was declared to the carrier so it travels insured. Chile only. |
| requires_document_return | boolean | The carrier was asked to bring back a sheet signed by the recipient at delivery. Chile only. |
| requires_pickup_on_delivery | boolean | A return label shipped inside the package, for the recipient to send a return later. Chile only, and consumer (D2C) orders only. |

All five are set at order creation and cannot be changed through `PUT /v1/orders/:id`. See **Create Order** for the eligibility rules and the error codes each one can return.

**They record a request, not a confirmation.** The carrier's emission response says nothing about these services, so these fields report what Cubbo asked for on your behalf. Two of them leave visible evidence: the signed-document return's sheet and the return label both arrive as extra pages inside the order's label PDF.

### Pagination

`page` (default `1`) and `per_page` (default `10`, max **100** — a larger value is silently clamped to 100). The response carries a `meta` object; see the collection overview for its shape and for how to detect the last page.

request.description:
Pick-and-ship (D2C) flow: creates a `pending` order **and immediately generates its shipping labels** in a single call. Only for pick&ship stores.

### Body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `store_id` | integer | yes | |
| `order_number` | string | yes | |
| `shipping_method_id` | integer | one-of | Provide this **or** `integration_shipping_method` (exactly one). |
| `integration_shipping_method` | string | one-of | |
| `shipping` | object | yes | `first_name` (min 3), `address1` (min 3), `country`, `city`, `province` required; `zip_code` required when the warehouse requires it; `last_name, phone, email, address2, interior_number` optional. |
| `products` | array | no | `{ sku, quantity }`. |
| `packages` | array | yes | `{ weight_kg (min 0.01), length_cm, width_cm, height_cm (min 1) }`. |

Returns an array of generated shipping labels (`ShippingLabelApiSerializer`). Errors: **422** (`MISSING_SHIPPING_METHOD`, `INVALID_SHIPPING_METHOD`, `MISSING_ZIP_CODE`, or `{ errors: [...] }` on order validation); **409** on throttle.

Lightweight, paginated order listing that returns only a caller-selected subset of fields via `fields[]` — a leaner alternative to `GET /orders`.

**Query params:** `store_id` (required), `page`, `per_page`, `sort_by` (`id`, `order_date`, `channel_created_at`, `shipping_date`, `updated_at`), `sort` (`asc`/`desc`), `status[]`, `order_type[]`, `shipping_email`, `normalized_shipping_phone_suffix` (min 3 digits), `fields[]`.

Unknown names are ignored; empty/omitted returns all fields.

**Responses**

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 200 | `{ "orders": [...], "meta": {...} }` with pagination meta |
| 401 | Unknown `store_id` or no access |
| 422 | Param validation error |

### `delivery_tracking` fields

When `delivery_tracking` is included in `fields[]`, it is an array with **one entry per package** (deduplicated by tracking number; a single-package order has one entry). Each entry:

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shipping_number` | string or `null` | Carrier tracking/waybill number. |
| `tracking_url` | string or `null` | Carrier tracking URL. |
| `cubbo_tracking_url` | string | Cubbo-hosted tracking URL. |
| `service_id` | string or `null` | Carrier service identifier. |
| `shipping_status` | string or `null` | The package's shipping status. |
| `package_index` | integer | 1-based index of this package within the order. |
| `total_packages` | integer | Total number of packages in the order. |

`is_multi_package` (boolean) indicates whether the order ships as multiple independently-tracked packages.

**The return label is not a package.** An order that shipped with `requires_pickup_on_delivery` carries a second Blue Express label inside the box, for the recipient to send a return later. It is not a package of this shipment, so it is absent from `delivery_tracking` and does not count towards `total_packages` or `is_multi_package` — a single-package order with the service still reports one entry.

### Complementary services

`is_cod` is the collect-at-delivery flag, and `cod_amount` is the amount the carrier is instructed to collect when it differs from the order's value — `null` when there is no such override, in which case the order's full value is collected. `has_carrier_insurance` records whether the shipment was declared to the carrier as insured. `requires_document_return` records whether the carrier was asked to bring back a sheet signed by the recipient at delivery. `requires_pickup_on_delivery` records whether a return label shipped inside the package.

All five are set at order creation; see **Create Order** for the rules and the error codes. Note that they record what was **requested** of the carrier, not a confirmation from it.

request.description:
This API endpoint makes an HTTP GET request to retrieve inventory information for specific products in a store. The request includes the store ID and a list of SKUs for the products to be queried.

### Stock Status Definition

- **IN_WAREHOUSE:** All items physically present in the warehouse, including reserved, expired, damaged, in reception, active, etc.
    
- **AVAILABLE:** All items available for sale (ACTIVE + pre-sale). This is the quantity to be displayed in the store.
    
- **UNAVAILABLE**: Inventory physically in the warehouse but not available for sale; includes buffer stock, reserved for returns, damaged, held, and expired.
    
- **ACTIVE:** Items available for sale, excluding buffer stock.
    
- **DAMAGED:** All damaged items.
    
- **EXPIRED**: All items expired.
    
- **RECEPTION:** All items received and pending put away.
    
- **RESERVED:** All items reserved, whether for orders or returns (includes presale).
    
- **RESERVED_BY_ORDERS:** Stock reserved by orders.
    
- **RESERVED_BY_RETURNS**: Stock reserved for return orders.
    
- **RECEPTION-INCOMING-SELL-AHEAD:** All pre-sale items currently in the reception process that are available for sale but have not yet been stored in inventory.
    
- **RESERVED-RECEPTION-INCOMING-SELL-AHEAD**: All pre-sale items currently in the reception process, reserved for orders, but have not yet been stored in inventory
    
- **RESERVED-INCOMING-SELL-AHEAD**: All pre-sale items reserved for orders that have not yet been stored in inventory.
    
- **INCOMING-SELL-AHEAD**: All pre-sale items available for sale that have not yet been stored in inventory.
    
- **RESERVED-WITHOUT-SELL-AHEAD**: All reserved items that do not include pre-sale items.
    
- **BUFFER_STOCK**: Quantity of stock per product set aside to be used in case of overselling.
    
- **OUT_OF_STOCK**: All missing items needed to complete orders in backorder status.
    

### Pagination

`page` (default `1`) and `per_page` (default `10`, max **200** — a larger value returns `422`). The response carries a `meta` object; see the collection overview for its shape.

### Description

Returns the lots of a **single product**, with each lot's status, expiration date and stock. The store is taken from your credential — there is no `store_id` parameter.

Use `GET /inventory` to sweep the whole catalogue; use this endpoint when you need one product's lots filtered or paginated.

### Query params

| Param | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sku` | string | see note | Exact SKU of the product. |
| `bar_code` | string | see note | Exact barcode of the product. |
| `lot_code` | string | no | Exact lot code — matches the lot's `lot_code` as returned here (for lots created through `POST /lots/upsert` with a `sku`, that is `{sku}-{lot_code}`). Not a substring search. |
| `status[]` | string or array | no | `ACTIVE`, `HOLDED`, `DAMAGED`, `EXPIRED`. Accepts a single value or repeated `status[]`. |
| `expiration_from` | date | no | `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive. |
| `expiration_to` | date | no | `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive. |
| `page` | integer | no | Defaults to `1`. Minimum `1`. |
| `per_page` | integer | no | Defaults to `25`. Minimum `1`, maximum `200` (over the max is a `422`). |

**You must send `sku` or `bar_code`.** Each call describes one product. If you send both, they must identify the same product — otherwise the response is `404`. Internal product ids are not accepted.

### Response `200 OK`

`product` describes the resolved product (`skus` is an array — a product can carry more than one SKU). `lots` carries one entry per lot, ordered by expiration date, soonest first; lots with no `expiration_date` sort **after** all dated lots. `expiration_date` is `null` when the lot has no expiration.

A product with no lots returns `"lots": []` and a `total_count` of `0` — that is a success, not an error.

**The `stock` keys**

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `AVAILABLE` | Sellable now. |
| `IN_WAREHOUSE` | Every unit physically at the warehouse regardless of status — the larger figure, including reserved, damaged, held and expired units. |
| `ACTIVE` | Units in `ACTIVE` status. |
| `RESERVED` | Assigned to orders. |
| `DAMAGED` | Units held as damaged. |
| `HOLDED` | Withheld by a lot hold. |
| `EXPIRED` | Units held as expired. |
| `SHIPPED` | Already left the warehouse. |
| `RECEPTION-INCOMING-SELL-AHEAD` | Arrived, still being received, sellable ahead. |
| `RESERVED-WITHOUT-SELL-AHEAD` | `RESERVED` excluding sell-ahead reservations. |
| `AVAILABLE_EXTERNALLY_CONFIRMED` / `AVAILABLE_NOT_EXTERNALLY_CONFIRMED` | `AVAILABLE` split by whether the replenishment that brought the units in has been confirmed by your system. If you do not use replenishment confirmation, ordinary stock lands in the `NOT_EXTERNALLY_CONFIRMED` bucket — but sell-ahead units always count as confirmed, so that bucket is not always empty. |

Variant **parent** products are not addressable here. Query the individual variant's SKU instead; a parent SKU returns `404`.

### Errors

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `401` | Missing, malformed or expired token, or the token lacks read access. |
| `404` | No product in your store matches the `sku` / `bar_code`. Because the store is derived from your token, a product belonging to another store is indistinguishable from one that does not exist. |
| `422` | Neither `sku` nor `bar_code` sent (`either sku or bar_code is required`); unknown `status`; malformed date; `per_page` over 200; or the identifier matches more than one product (`ambiguous identifier: it matches product ids ...`). |
| `500` | Unexpected error — safe to retry. |

### Related

`POST /lots/upsert` — create a lot or update its expiration date. `POST /lots/hold/store/:store_id` and `POST /lots/unhold/store/:store_id` — withhold a lot's stock from fulfilment, or release it.

request.description:
Find a replenishment by id

**Replenishment statuses:**

| **status** | **description** |
| --- | --- |
| WITHOUT_SCHEDULING | created but without schedule to be received |
| REQUESTED | awaiting arrival |
| PROCESSING | stock is being received |
| IN_PUTAWAY | stock is being located in picking bins |
| CANCELED | has been canceled |
| COMPLETED | stocks were received and are available for sale |

**Supplier invoices (facturas):**

`supplier_invoices` lists the captured supplier invoice (factura) numbers for the replenishment, sorted. The field is always present: `[]` when no facturas have been captured. Each entry is an object with an `invoice_number` (string).

`supplier_invoice_files` lists the documents uploaded during receiving (the factura PDF plus supporting documents). Always present: `[]` when none. It is a top-level array — files belong to the replenishment, not to a specific invoice number. Each entry:

```json
"supplier_invoice_files": [
  {
    "url": "https://<bucket>.s3.amazonaws.com/...&X-Amz-Expires=900...",
    "filename": "factura-F-12345.pdf",
    "content_type": "application/pdf",
    "byte_size": 123456,
    "expires_at": "2022-10-09T03:00:00Z"
  }
]
```

`url` is a presigned S3 link valid for **15 minutes** after the response is generated (`expires_at` is the exact cutoff). Download promptly, or call this endpoint again for fresh links. The replenishmentStatus webhook does not carry files — fetch them from this endpoint when an event arrives.

`received_by_invoice` (inside each `replenishment_products` entry) breaks that product's `received_quantity` down by supplier invoice:

```json
"received_by_invoice": [
  { "invoice_number": "F-12345", "quantity": 4000 },
  { "invoice_number": "F-12346", "quantity": 900 },
  { "invoice_number": null, "quantity": 100 }
]
```

Sorted by invoice number, with the `null` bucket last. `invoice_number: null` counts units received without a captured invoice (e.g. receptions before invoice capture was enabled for the warehouse). Per product, the quantities always sum to `received_quantity`. Quantities reflect what was physically received under each factura — not what the invoice document declared. After warehouse-side replenishment splits, an `invoice_number` can appear here that is not listed in `supplier_invoices`.

This webhook is sent when an order changes status within Cubbo's fulfillment flow. It allows you to track order progress through the different operational stages.

| `order_number` | string | Order number provided by the client when creating the order. |
| `status` | string | New order status. See possible values below. |
| `updated_at` | string (ISO 8601) | Date and time of the status change. |
| `store_id` | integer | Store identifier associated with the order. |

### Optional Fields

These fields may be included depending on your store's webhook configuration.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `products` | array | When `status` = `picking` | List of products being picked. Each item contains `id` (integer), `sku` (string), and `quantity` (integer). |
| `picking_status` | string | When `status` = `picking` | Sub-status of the picking process, if available. |
| `channel_integration_id` | integer | Enabled per store | Sales channel integration ID through which the order was received. |

| `shipped` | Handed off to the carrier. |
| `delivery` | Delivered to the recipient. |
| `canceled` | Order has been canceled. |
| `returned` | Order has been returned. |

request.description:
This webhook is sent when the carrier reports a change in the delivery status of the shipment. It allows you to receive real-time shipping updates.

### Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | string | Current shipping status. See possible values below. For multi-package orders, this describes the package that triggered the event. |
| `store_id` | integer | Store identifier. |
| `carrier_name` | string | Shipping carrier handling the delivery. |
| `tracking_urls` | array of strings | Cubbo tracking URLs. |
| `tracking_number` | string | Carrier tracking/waybill number of the triggering package. |
| `zip_code` | string | Destination zip/postal code. |
| `order_number` | string | Client order number. |
| `updated_at` | string (ISO 8601) | Date and time of the shipping status change. |
| `estimated_time_arrival` | string (ISO 8601) or `null` | Estimated delivery date. `null` when status is `shipment_returned` or `shipment_canceled`. |
| `incident_description` | string or `null` | Incident details. Only present when `status` is `shipment_with_incident`. |
| `is_multi_package` | boolean | Whether the order ships as multiple independently-tracked packages. |
| `packages` | array of objects | One entry per physical package (identified by tracking number). Each entry: `shipping_number`, `tracking_url`, `shipping_status`, `carrier_name`, `package_index`, `total_packages`. |
| `triggered_by_package` | object | The package whose tracking event triggered this webhook: `shipping_number`, `shipping_status`, `carrier_name`, `tracking_url`, `previous_status`, `package_index`, `total_packages`. |
| `label_tracking_event_id` | integer or `null` | ID of the per-package tracking event that produced this webhook. Use it to deduplicate/correlate. |

### Optional Fields

| Field | Type | Condition | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `channel_integration_id` | integer | Enabled per store | Sales channel integration ID. |
| `channel_order_id` | string | Enabled per store | Order ID in the original sales channel. |
| `channel_name` | string | Enabled per store | Name of the sales channel (e.g., `Shopify`, `VTEX`, `MercadoLibre`). |

### Possible Shipping Statuses

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `shipment_created` | Shipping label has been generated. |
| `awaiting_collection` | Package is waiting to be collected by the carrier. |
| `shipment_collected` | Carrier has collected the package from the warehouse. |
| `shipment_in_transit` | Package is in transit to its destination. |
| `shipment_out_for_delivery` | Package is out for delivery to the recipient. |
| `shipment_delivered` | Package has been delivered successfully. |
| `shipment_with_incident` | Shipment has an incident. See `incident_description` for details. |
| `shipment_to_be_self_collected` | Package is available for pickup at a collection point. |
| `shipment_returned` | Package has been returned to the Cubbo warehouse. |
| `shipment_canceled` | Shipment has been canceled. |

### Multi-package orders

When an order ships as multiple packages, `is_multi_package` is `true` and `packages` lists every package (deduplicated by tracking number — one entry per physical package). The top-level `status`, `tracking_number` and `carrier_name`, along with `triggered_by_package`, describe the specific package whose tracking changed. Each entry's `shipping_status` reflects that package's own status.

### Example: Shipment with Incident

```
{

  "store_id": 1,
  "carrier_name": "FedEx",
  "tracking_urls": ["https://tracking.cubbo.com/XYZ789"],

  "updated_at": "2026-03-12T16:45:00-06:00",
  "estimated_time_arrival": null,
  "incident_description": "Recipient not available at delivery address"
}

 ```

request.description:
This webhook is sent when available inventory levels change for one or more products. It delivers a full stock snapshot of the affected products, allowing you to keep your systems synchronized with Cubbo's warehouse inventory. Triggers include: order shipments, cancellations, returns, stock receiving (replenishments), and stock adjustments.

### **Fields**

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| event | string | Event type. Always `inventoryMovement`. |
| occurred_at | string (ISO 8601) | Date and time when the inventory snapshot was taken. |
| sequence | integer | Monotonically increasing sequence number per integration. Use to detect ordering and gaps. |
| store_id | integer | Store identifier. |
| products | array\[object\] | List of products with updated inventory. |
| products\[\].product_name | string | Product name. |
| products\[\].skus | array\[string\] | All SKU codes associated with the product. |
| products\[\].quantity | integer | Current available stock quantity (sellable units, excluding reserved/damaged). |
| products\[\].product_code | string or null | Product bar code. May be null. |
| products\[\].units | array\[object\] | Optional. Per-unit serial/IMEI. Present only for unit-code products (absent for non-unit-code damaged/lost units). |
| products\[\].units\[\].unit_code | string | Optional. Per-unit serial/IMEI. Present only for unit-code products (absent for non-unit-code damaged/lost units). |
| products\[\].units\[\].status | string | Unit status: ACTIVE, RESERVED, DAMAGED, LOST. |
| products\[\].units\[\].damaged_source | string | Optional. Origin of the damage; present only when `status = DAMAGED` (e.g. STORAGE, RETURN, REPLENISHMENT). |
| products\[\].units\[\].lost_source | string | Optional. Origin of the loss; present only when `status = LOST` (e.g. RETURN, REPLENISHMENT). |
| products\[\].lots | array\[object\] | Optional. Lot/expiration breakdown. Present only for expiration-tracked products; lists only lots with available stock, sorted FEFO (earliest expiry first). |
| products\[\].lots\[\].lot_code | string | Lot unique code. |
| products\[\].lots\[\].expiration_date | string (ISO8601) or null | Lot expiration date. May be null. |
| products\[\].lots\[\].quantity | integer | Available units in this lot. |

#### **Additional Header**

| Header | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| X-Cubbo-Idempotency-Key | string (UUID) | Unique key for receiver-side deduplication. Store processed keys and skip duplicates on retries. |

#### **Sequence Numbers**

The `sequence` field is a monotonically increasing integer that never resets. Since each event contains a full stock snapshot (not a delta), the event with the highest sequence number always represents the most current inventory state. If events arrive out of order, only apply the one with the highest sequence.

#### **Retry Behavior**

If your endpoint does not respond with a `2xx` status code, Cubbo retries up to 5 times with exponential backoff. `400 Bad Request` responses are not retried. If all retries are exhausted, the event is dropped. The next inventory change triggers a new webhook with the latest stock snapshot.

request.description:
This webhook is sent when a replenishment (inbound inventory shipment) changes status in Cubbo's warehouse — as stock arrives and is received, put away, and completed, or when the replenishment is canceled. It lets you track your inbound inventory in real time.

This event is opt-in per integration: it requires a dedicated replenishment webhook URL and must be activated by Cubbo. Contact us to enable it.

### **Fields**

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| event | string | Event type. Always `replenishmentStatus`. |
| occurred_at | string (ISO 8601) | Date and time when the event was generated. |
| sequence | integer | Ordering hint: the status transition's timestamp in epoch milliseconds. Increases with each transition but is NOT contiguous — use it to detect ordering, not gaps. |
| store_id | integer | Store identifier. |
| replenishment_id | integer | Replenishment identifier in Cubbo. |
| status | string | New replenishment status. See possible values below. |
| products | array\[object\] | Products in the replenishment. Omitted when `status` = `CANCELED`. |
| products\[\].product_code | string or null | Product bar code. May be null. |
| products\[\].skus | array\[string\] | All SKU codes associated with the product. |
| products\[\].expected_quantity | integer | Units announced for this product in the replenishment. |
| products\[\].received_quantity | integer | Units actually received so far. |
| supplier_invoices | array\[object\] | Captured supplier invoice (factura) numbers for the replenishment, sorted. Always present for non-CANCELED events: `[]` when none. Omitted when `status` = `CANCELED`. |
| supplier_invoices\[\].invoice_number | string | Supplier invoice (factura) number. |

### Possible Replenishment Statuses

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `PROCESSING` | Stock has arrived and is being received at the warehouse. |
| `IN_PUTAWAY` | Received stock is being placed into warehouse locations. |
| `COMPLETED` | Replenishment has been fully processed. |
| `CANCELED` | Replenishment has been canceled. |

Not every replenishment emits every status — some records start directly at a later stage and emit only the later events.

#### **Additional Headers**

| Header | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| X-Webhook-Event | string | Always `replenishmentStatus`. |
| X-Cubbo-Idempotency-Key | string | Deterministic key (`replenishment:<replenishment_id>:<status>:<integration_id>`) for receiver-side deduplication. Retries of the same event reuse the same key — store processed keys and skip duplicates. |

#### **Ordering**

Events for the same integration are delivered one at a time (FIFO). If events still arrive out of order, apply the one with the highest `sequence` for a given `replenishment_id`.

#### **Retry Behavior**

If your endpoint does not respond with a `2xx` status code, Cubbo retries up to 5 times with exponential backoff. Retries carry the same `X-Cubbo-Idempotency-Key`, so duplicates can be detected and skipped.

item.description:
## Webhook Signatures & Validation

We sign every webhook outgoing request using a hash-based message authentication code (HMAC) with SHA-256.

### Webhook Request Headers

| Header | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Content-Type` | Always `application/json`. |
| `Accept` | Always `application/json`. |
| `isa` | Issued at timestamp (Unix epoch). Creation date of the request. |
| `exp` | Expiration timestamp (Unix epoch). Five minutes after `isa`. A webhook message with an expired signature must be discarded. |
| `X-Cubbo-Hmac-SHA256` | Digital signature. Generate the same hash and compare it to verify the message has not been tampered with. |
| `X-Cubbo-Webhook-Message-Id` | Request's unique identifier (UUID). Useful to check if the webhook was already processed (deduplication). |
| `X-Webhook-Event` | The event type: `orderFulfilled`, `orderUpdated`, `shippingUpdated`, `inventoryMovement`, or `replenishmentStatus`. |

### Digital Signature

Each digital signature is generated using HMAC with SHA-256:

1. Create the `signed_payload` string by concatenating with `.` as separator:
    
    - `X-Cubbo-Webhook-Message-Id`
        
    - `isa` timestamp
        
    - `exp` timestamp
        
    - The actual JSON payload (request body, with keys sorted alphabetically)
        

```
Result: `{X-Cubbo-Webhook-Message-Id}.{isa}.{exp}.{json_body}`

 ```

1. Generate the HMAC using the provided `consumer_secret` as the key and the `signed_payload` string as the message.
    
2. Compare the resulting hex digest with the `X-Cubbo-Hmac-SHA256` header value.

## Webhook Events

Cubbo sends webhook events for order, shipping, inventory, and replenishment lifecycle changes. Each request includes the event type in the `X-Webhook-Event` header.

Each event is documented as a `POST` request in this folder, showing exactly what Cubbo sends to your endpoint. To smoke-test your receiver, set the `your_webhook_url` variable to your own endpoint and fire the example — note that the HMAC signature headers are only generated by Cubbo, so manual test requests will not carry a valid signature.

| Event | `X-Webhook-Event` value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Order Status Update | `orderUpdated` | Sent when an order changes status within Cubbo's operational flow. |
| Order Fulfilled | `orderFulfilled` | Sent when an order is fulfilled: a shipping label is generated and the order is ready for carrier pickup. |

### Description

Partial update of the store bound to your credential. **Accepts no store id** — the store is resolved from the Open API integration credential in your token, so use the `client_id` / `client_secret` that `POST /stores` returned for that store. | `description` | string | Free text. |

| `state` | string | For a store operating in Brazil, a two-letter UF code such as `SP` — anything else is a `422`. Case-insensitive on input; stored upper-case. This field decides whether a sale is treated as intrastate or interstate, so a wrong value has fiscal consequences. |
| `tax_company_name` | string | Razão social. |
| `tax_address` | string | Fiscal address — logradouro. |
| `tax_address_number` | string | Número. |
| `tax_address_neighborhood` | string | Bairro. |
| `tax_city` | string | Município. |
| `tax_zipcode` | string | CEP. |
| `tax_state_registration` | string | Inscrição estadual. |
| `tax_state_phone` | string | Contact phone on fiscal documents. |

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `401` | Token missing, invalid, or not bound to a store. |

| Field | Type | Description |

### Description

Uploads the A1 digital certificate of the store bound to your credential and sets its NF-e numbering in the same call. **Accepts no store id** — the store is resolved from the Open API integration credential in your token, so use the `client_id` / `client_secret` that `POST /stores` returned for that store.

Requires the store's fiscal account (`POST /store/fiscal-account`) to exist already.

This is also the endpoint you use to upload a **renewed** certificate.

**The numbering is overwritten on every call.** If you send `next_invoice_number: 1` for a store that has already issued NF-e, its counter is reset and every subsequent invoice is rejected by SEFAZ as a duplicate. On a renewal, send the store's current numbering — do not restart it.

The certificate and its password are sent on to the fiscal provider only: they never reach a log, an error report, or this endpoint's response.

**Not guaranteed atomic.** The certificate and the numbering go to the provider in one request, but the provider does not document that request as all-or-nothing. A rejection of either field is reported to you; it is not proof that the other was rolled back, so confirm the store's series and next number with Cubbo before retrying.

### Body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `certificate_base64` | string | yes | The `.pfx` / `.p12` file, Base64-encoded. |
| `certificate_password` | string | yes | Password of the certificate. |

item.description:
These are the error codes used in this API:

401 - Unauthorized -> It means that the request is not authorized correctly or that your user doesn't have enough permissions to access that resource.

422 - Unprocessable Entity -> You will get these error if the content of your request is wrong. The request will be accompanied by an error message explaining what went wrong. These message will be found in the "error" property.

200,201 -> Your request was executed succesfully

500 -> Internal Server Error -> Unexpected Error, please write us at integraciones@cubbo.com with an example of your request.

429 - Too Many Requests -> You exceeded a rate limit. See "Rate limits" below.

## Rate limits

| Limit | Scope | On exceeding |
|-------|-------|--------------|
| 60 requests / minute to `POST /v1/auth/token` | Per `client_id` | `429` with a `Retry-After` header |
| 600 requests / minute to every other `/v1/*` endpoint | Per `client_id` | `429` with a `Retry-After` header |
| 30 requests / 30 seconds to `POST /v1/auth/token` | Per source IP | `429`, and your IP is blocked for 10 minutes |

The two per-`client_id` limits return `{ "error": "Too many requests. Please slow down and try again later." }` plus a `Retry-After` header holding the number of seconds to wait.

The per-IP limit is enforced at our edge, before the request reaches the API. It returns a `429` **without** that JSON body, and it keeps rejecting requests from your IP for 10 minutes — so it is the one worth avoiding.

### Staying under them

- **Cache your access token.** Request one token and reuse it for its full `expires_in` (up to 24 h). Requesting a fresh token on every call is the most common cause of a `429`.
- **Back off on a 429.** Wait the seconds given in `Retry-After` (or 60 s if the header is absent) before retrying. Retrying immediately keeps the bucket full.
- **Batch where the API allows it** — e.g. `Get inventory for a list of SKUs` and `Get Orders With Fields` take many records per request.

request.description:
Lists Click & Collect pickup locations near a postal code, across every carrier Cubbo supports (Cubbo pickup network, DHL, Estafeta). **No authentication required.**

Use a `service_code` from this response as `click_and_collect_service_code` when creating an order, or as `service_code` in **Convert Order to Click & Collect**.

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `postal_code` | string | yes | Buyer postal code to search around. |
| `address` | string | no | Street and number; some carriers use it to refine the search. |

**Response 200:** `{ "rates": [ { "service_name", "service_code", "source", "description" } ] }`

- `service_name` is a display string in Spanish (distance, location name, and opening hours when the carrier provides them).
- `source` and `description` both carry the location address.
- An empty `rates` array means no locations were found near that postal code.

Need structured fields (carrier, distance, schedule) or eligibility for a specific order? Use **List Pickup Points for an Order**.

request.description:
Converts a home-delivery order into a Click & Collect order to the chosen pickup point. Rewrites the shipping method and destination; the order is reprocessed automatically. Mexico, national shipping only.

Requires Bearer auth and the orders-update permission.

**Body (JSON)**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `store_id` | integer | yes | Store that owns the order. |
| `service_code` | string | yes | `service_code` of the chosen point, as returned by **List Pickup Points for an Order**. |

**Response 200:** the full order (same shape as other v1 order responses) with `is_click_and_collect: true` and `click_and_collect_metadata`.

**Errors:** 404 `ORDER_NOT_FOUND` / `store_not_found` as in the listing. Business rejections are **422** `{ "error": "<message>", "code": "<CODE>" }`:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `INVALID_ORDER_STATUS` | The order is past the point where it can be converted (label/packing). |
| `ALREADY_CLICK_AND_COLLECT` | Already converted. The body includes the current `click_and_collect_metadata` (public fields only, may be null on old orders) so a retrying client can reconcile. |
| `INVALID_CNC_SERVICE_CODE` | Unknown or stale `service_code`. List the points again and use a fresh one. |
| `STORE_EDIT_RESTRICTED` | The store's edit window does not allow changing this order. |
| `CNC_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_STORE` | Click & Collect is not enabled for the store. |
| `CNC_CARRIER_NOT_ENABLED_FOR_STORE` | The point's carrier is not enabled for the store. |
| `CNC_CARRIER_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE` | The point's carrier is temporarily disabled. Pick a point from another carrier. |
| `CNC_LOCATION_CONFIRMATION_FAILED` | The carrier could not confirm the point. Retry or pick another point. |
| `CNC_SHIPPING_METHOD_NOT_FOUND` | Click & Collect shipping setup is incomplete for the store. Contact support. |
| `CNC_PRICE_EXCEEDS_ORIGINAL` | The Click & Collect rate exceeds the order's original rate (skipped when the store's C&C config waives the price check). |
| `CNC_ORIGINAL_NOT_CUBBO_BILLED` | The order ships on an external label (e.g. Mercado Envíos, Amazon) and cannot be converted. |
| `CNC_ORIGINAL_NOT_NATIONAL_SHIPPING` | The original shipping method is not national. |
| `CNC_RATE_CARD_UNAVAILABLE` | The store's rate for this order could not be resolved. Contact support. |

This list is not exhaustive; treat unknown 422 codes as a non-retryable rejection.
